header.title: Curse tablets from Germania superior (Epigraphic Database Heidelberg): AI translation (Claude)
header.author: Latin curse tablets
header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's urn:defix:edh:germania-superior:lat, from the Epigraphic Database Heidelberg (CC BY-SA 4.0), one English line for each line of the original. Only some passages are translated so far: those that the Atlas of Ancient Myth, Magic in the Ancient Texts and the demons-and-angels study cite.
header.statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.

notes.52181.2.5: The first two lines end a different tablet (52181). 'aginat' is a rare verb, roughly 'busies himself, contrives'. 'per benedictum tuum' may mean 'by your blessing' or 'by your blessed one'. Restorations of a letter or two inside otherwise legible words are not marked in the English.
notes.4630.1.1: Two tablets (4630, 4633). 'M()[a]rius' carries an unexpanded abbreviation; the first part of the name is uncertain. 'Consularem' may be a personal name (Consularis) or a title ('the ex-consul'). 'tanquam nullo' is marked as faulty in both words; the sense ('as if a nobody among the dead'?) is uncertain. Restorations of a letter or two inside otherwise legible words are not marked in the English.
notes.76472.2.1: Several tablets (76472, 76474, 76476). 'IA' and 'ICLVM' cannot be read as words. Genitives after names are taken as fathers' names; they could also name owners. 'Ornatus()' and 'Senopatium()' are unexpanded abbreviations, the latter marked as faulty. In the last line 'Valentinus' is marked as an error, probably for 'Valentis' ('[son] of Valens', as in the line before), and the tablet writes 'quomodo' ('just as') as COMDI.
notes.52180.4: '[...]EMESMANT()' cannot be read as a word; it ends in an unexpanded abbreviation. 'Atthis' is marked as an error for Attis. 'cistas penetrales' are taken as the sacred chests kept in the inner sanctuary.
notes.54661.2.19: The first two lines end another tablet and contain erased letters ([[.]]); only 'mancas' ('maimed', feminine plural) can be read. 'habiatis', 'quit' and 'aget' are irregular spellings, read as habeatis, quid and agit.
notes.76518.2.2: Several tablets (76518, 76519, 76521). 'Haeb()' is an unexpanded abbreviation followed by a loss; the name cannot be completed. 76521 holds only damaged names.
